hints: Determine which particle pulls the system: compare the downhill components of weight: for $B$, $1.2g\sin 30^\circ = 6\text{ N}$; for $A$, $0.8g\sin 45^\circ = 0.8(10)\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \approx 5.657\text{ N}$. Since $6 > 5.657$, particle $B$ accelerates down its slope and $A$ accelerates up its slope.
Write the equations of motion using $F_{\text{net}} = ma$ for each particle: $T - 0.8g\sin 45^\circ = 0.8a$ and $1.2g\sin 30^\circ - T = 1.2a$.
Add the equations to eliminate $T$ and solve for the common acceleration $a$.
Use the constant-acceleration formula $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 0$ and $s = 0.4\text{ m}$ to calculate $v$.
walkthrough:
Compare the components of weight along the respective faces to determine the direction of acceleration:
$$\text{For } B: \quad m_B g\sin 30^\circ = 1.2(10)(0.5) = 6\text{ N}$$
$$\text{For } A: \quad m_A g\sin 45^\circ = 0.8(10)\sin 45^\circ = 8\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 4\sqrt{2} \approx 5.6569\text{ N}$$
Since $6 > 5.6569$, particle $B$ moves down its $30^\circ$ slope and particle $A$ moves up its $45^\circ$ slope with common acceleration $a$.

Form the equations of motion for both particles:
$$\text{For } A: \quad T - 0.8g\sin 45^\circ = 0.8a \implies T - 4\sqrt{2} = 0.8a$$
$$\text{For } B: \quad 1.2g\sin 30^\circ - T = 1.2a \implies 6 - T = 1.2a$$

Add the two equations to eliminate $T$ and solve for $a$:
$$(6 - T) + (T - 4\sqrt{2}) = 1.2a + 0.8a$$
$$6 - 4\sqrt{2} = 2.0a$$
$$6 - 5.65685 = 0.34315 = 2.0a \implies a = \frac{0.34315}{2} \approx 0.17157\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Use the SUVAT relation $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ from rest ($u = 0$) over distance $s = 0.4\text{ m}$:
$$v^2 = 0 + 2(0.17157)(0.4) = 0.13726$$
$$v = \sqrt{0.13726} \approx 0.370\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Check the net driving force to establish the direction of motion:
Weight component of $B$ down its $30^\circ$ slope:
$$W_{B,\parallel} = m_B g\sin 30^\circ = 1.2 \times 10 \times 0.5 = 6\text{ N}$$
Weight component of $A$ down its $45^\circ$ slope:
$$W_{A,\parallel} = m_A g\sin 45^\circ = 0.8 \times 10 \times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = 4\sqrt{2} \approx 5.65685\text{ N}$$
Since $6 > 4\sqrt{2}$, particle $B$ accelerates downwards along the $30^\circ$ slope and particle $A$ accelerates upwards along the $45^\circ$ slope.

State Newton's second law for each particle along its respective plane of motion:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
For particle $A$ moving uphill:
$$T - m_A g\sin 45^\circ = m_A a \implies T - 4\sqrt{2} = 0.8a$$
For particle $B$ moving downhill:
$$m_B g\sin 30^\circ - T = m_B a \implies 6 - T = 1.2a$$

Add the two equations to eliminate the internal tension $T$:
$$(6 - T) + (T - 4\sqrt{2}) = 1.2a + 0.8a$$
$$6 - 4\sqrt{2} = 2a$$
$$6 - 5.65685 = 0.34315 = 2a$$
Divide both sides by $2$:
$$a = \frac{0.34315}{2} = 0.171575\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

State the SUVAT velocity-displacement formula:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$
Both particles start from rest ($u = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$) and travel a distance of $s = 0.4\text{ m}$:
$$v^2 = 0^2 + 2 \times 0.171575 \times 0.4$$
$$v^2 = 0.8 \times 0.171575 = 0.13726$$
Take the square root:
$$v = \sqrt{0.13726} \approx 0.37049 \approx 0.370\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: At limiting equilibrium with impending motion in the direction established in part (i), $B$ tends to slide down and $A$ tends to slide up, so friction on $B$ acts up its slope ($F_B$) and friction on $A$ acts down its slope ($F_A$).
Calculate the normal reactions perpendicular to the faces: $R_A = 0.8g\cos 45^\circ = 4\sqrt{2}$ and $R_B = 1.2g\cos 30^\circ = 6\sqrt{3}$.
Express the limiting friction forces in terms of $\mu$: $F_A = \mu R_A = 4\sqrt{2}\mu$ and $F_B = \mu R_B = 6\sqrt{3}\mu$.
Set up the equilibrium equation for the whole connected system: $1.2g\sin 30^\circ - 0.8g\sin 45^\circ = F_A + F_B$, and solve for $\mu$.
walkthrough: Because the tendency of motion is for $B$ to slide downwards and $A$ to slide upwards, limiting friction opposes this impending motion: friction $F_A$ on $A$ acts downwards along its $45^\circ$ slope and friction $F_B$ on $B$ acts upwards along its $30^\circ$ slope.

Resolve forces perpendicular to each face to find the normal contact reactions:
$$R_A = 0.8g\cos 45^\circ = 8\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 4\sqrt{2}\text{ N}$$
$$R_B = 1.2g\cos 30^\circ = 12\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 6\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$

Write the limiting friction expressions:
$$F_A = \mu R_A = 4\sqrt{2}\mu$$
$$F_B = \mu R_B = 6\sqrt{3}\mu$$

Write equilibrium equations parallel to the planes for each particle:
$$\text{For } A: \quad T = 0.8g\sin 45^\circ + F_A = 4\sqrt{2} + 4\sqrt{2}\mu$$
$$\text{For } B: \quad T = 1.2g\sin 30^\circ - F_B = 6 - 6\sqrt{3}\mu$$

Equate the two expressions for tension $T$ to eliminate $T$ and solve for $\mu$:
$$4\sqrt{2} + 4\sqrt{2}\mu = 6 - 6\sqrt{3}\mu$$
$$(6\sqrt{3} + 4\sqrt{2})\mu = 6 - 4\sqrt{2}$$
$$\mu = \frac{6 - 4\sqrt{2}}{6\sqrt{3} + 4\sqrt{2}} = \frac{6 - 5.65685}{10.39230 + 5.65685} = \frac{0.34315}{16.04915} \approx 0.0214$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Determine the directions of limiting friction forces:
As found in part (i), the driving component of $B$ ($6\text{ N}$) exceeds that of $A$ ($4\sqrt{2} \approx 5.657\text{ N}$). Therefore, impending motion is for $B$ to slide downwards and $A$ to slide upwards.
By Newton's third law and friction principles, the friction force on $A$ opposes uphill motion (acts down the $45^\circ$ slope), and on $B$ opposes downhill motion (acts up the $30^\circ$ slope).

Resolve forces perpendicular to each face in equilibrium:
For particle $A$ on the $45^\circ$ incline:
$$R_A = m_A g\cos 45^\circ = 0.8 \times 10 \times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = 4\sqrt{2}\text{ N}$$
For particle $B$ on the $30^\circ$ incline:
$$R_B = m_B g\cos 30^\circ = 1.2 \times 10 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 6\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$

Apply the limiting friction formula $F = \mu R$ for each particle:
$$F_A = \mu R_A = 4\sqrt{2}\mu$$
$$F_B = \mu R_B = 6\sqrt{3}\mu$$

Form the equilibrium equations parallel to each face:
For particle $A$:
$$T - m_A g\sin 45^\circ - F_A = 0 \implies T = 4\sqrt{2} + 4\sqrt{2}\mu$$
For particle $B$:
$$m_B g\sin 30^\circ - T - F_B = 0 \implies T = 6 - 6\sqrt{3}\mu$$

Equate the two expressions for $T$:
$$4\sqrt{2} + 4\sqrt{2}\mu = 6 - 6\sqrt{3}\mu$$
Collect terms containing $\mu$ on the left-hand side and constants on the right-hand side:
$$4\sqrt{2}\mu + 6\sqrt{3}\mu = 6 - 4\sqrt{2}$$
$$(6\sqrt{3} + 4\sqrt{2})\mu = 6 - 4\sqrt{2}$$
Divide both sides by $(6\sqrt{3} + 4\sqrt{2})$:
$$\mu = \frac{6 - 4\sqrt{2}}{6\sqrt{3} + 4\sqrt{2}}$$

Evaluate the intermediate numerical values:
$$4\sqrt{2} = 4 \times 1.414214 = 5.656854$$
$$6\sqrt{3} = 6 \times 1.732051 = 10.392305$$
$$\text{Numerator}: \quad 6 - 5.656854 = 0.343146$$
$$\text{Denominator}: \quad 10.392305 + 5.656854 = 16.049159$$
Compute the quotient:
$$\mu = \frac{0.343146}{16.049159} \approx 0.02138 \approx 0.0214$$
